instructions.question: Does the tweet lean positive or negative in feeling, or does it have no noticeable lean (neutral)?
instructions.rule: If the author shows a noticeable personal lean, choose it: wanting, looking forward to, enjoying or praising something is positive; letdowns, sighs, sadness, envy, critical digs or insults are negative. News of clear success (wins, records, awards) is positive; news of clear harm (injury, death, crash, charge, delay, dispute) is negative. Choose neutral for plain information, ads, listings, stats, matter-of-fact activity reports ('leaving tomorrow', 'might watch X tonight'), 'who's going?' questions without excitement words, and playful banter or jokes where the author isn't really pleased or upset.

neutral.what: No noticeable lean: plain information, ads, schedules, stats, headlines without clear outcome, questions, flat activity reports, and light banter or jokes without real pleasure or upset.
examples: Anyone wanna buy a Zac Brown Band ticket for the 3rd?
Might just watch the 3rd season of American Horror Story tonight
Who going with me to Knott's Saturday?
Ebola nurse may have been sick before taking the plane
neutral.cues: selling, tickets, specials, scheduled, reportedly, 'may' speculation, game stats, might, who's going
neutral.not_for: Personal tweets with a noticeable pleasant lean (positive) or a letdown, sigh or dig (negative).

positive.what: Noticeable pleasant lean: anticipation of plans or treats, enjoyment, liking, praise, pride, affection, tributes, or news of a clear success.
examples: I want IHOP tomorrow morning
In the car on our way to Milton Keynes to see the Foo Fighters tomorrow. #foofighters #miltonkeynes
8th strikeout of the afternoon for David Price's 100th career win!
Sending my sincere prayers & condolences to the Gifford family on Frank Gifford's passing. May he rest in peace.
positive.cues: want, can't wait, love, glad, fun, excited, proud, wins, beats, honored, !
positive.not_for: Dry ads, listings, or flat activity reports and 'who's going?' questions (neutral).

negative.what: Noticeable unpleasant lean: letdowns, frustration, sadness, envy, insults, critical digs, fear, or news of clear harm or failure.
examples: Might not be able to get a free taco tomorrow. As Napoleon Dynamite would say, dang it!
Just remembered I'm taking the PSSAs tomorrow. #Fml
RT @user Gavin Henson looks set to miss the Rugby World Cup after dislocating a bone in his right wrist yesterday
negative.cues: dang it, Argh, why oh why, sad, not happy, worst, sucks, hate, #Fml, injured, delayed
negative.not_for: Flat factual reports or playful teasing without real upset (neutral); warm tributes, or mixed tweets whose main point is excitement (positive).
